A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRFs++ research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial layout changes and added experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original kernel-approximation and timing experiments, graph classification, node clustering and mesh-normal prediction, including additional results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds image classification, GraphGPS experiments, additional kernel evaluations and mesh-runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Alongside the retained GRFs++ estimator, v2 introduces substantive model adaptations: normalized grid-kernel masks added to ViT attention and projected, summed eight-dimensional GRFs++ representations for GraphGPS (Appendices B.5 and C). Section 2.2.2 also reverses the printed termination inequality from <= to >=; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet and Places365 image classification, COLLAB and REDDIT-MULTI-12K graph classification, and supervised GraphGPS evaluations including PATTERN, CLUSTER and MNIST. CIFAR-10 and Peptides, previously used as sources of graphs for kernel estimation, also receive supervised prediction evaluations. These additions substantially broaden the tasks and represented data.

E2.justification: Comparisons expand beyond GRF and exact diffusion to 20 graph kernels and four GNNs across Tables 8-9, four additional clustering methods in Table 11, and Al Mohy's matrix-exponential algorithm in Table 10. ViT and Performer controls are added for the new applications. Appendix B.2 explicitly attributes the external kernel/GNN scores to Nikolentzos et al.; they are not documented as new baseline runs.

E3.justification: New protocols include ViT validation-set top-1 accuracy with degree-2 masks and mask strength 0.5, GraphGPS comparisons using a Performer backbone without default positional encoding, fixed-degree non-diffusion kernel tests, and runtime evaluation on meshes up to 35,300 vertices. The existing 10-fold graph-classification protocol and 80% mesh-normal masking remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 adds a substantial generality study across three non-diffusion kernels, including downstream classification using exp(W^2). Figure 6 and Table 1 add mesh-size scaling analyses against exact kernel computation. Earlier long-distance, termination-policy and walk-reuse analyses remain; v1 Figure 4 is incorporated into v2 Figure 5(a).

E5.justification: V2 Tables 8-9 newly report classification means with standard deviations, whereas v1 Figure 6 presented these comparisons without uncertainty. The existing ten repetitions for kernel experiments and 10-fold classification evaluation remain. No increased run count, new seed specification or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive transformer, runtime, non-diffusion-kernel and baseline results. For example, Table 3 reports ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.10 for ViT and 80.31 for GRF++. Original clustering and mesh scores remain unchanged. A retained classification ranking changes: GRF++ exceeds exact diffusion on REDDIT-BINARY in v1 Figure 6, but falls below it in v2 Figure 4/Table 9, which reports 84.4 versus 85.6.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.2 and Appendix A.2 replace E[X1^2] with E[X1^T X1] in the MSE formula and revise the proof's symmetry argument accordingly. Section 2.1 adds boundedness to the convergence assumption, and Section 2.2.1 restores the missing lambda^p factor in the diffusion modulation function. These correct existing mathematics without replacing the principal theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims of efficient, accurate and unbiased kernel approximation through walk stitching and flexible termination. The introduction expands the advertised downstream contribution to include image classification, modestly broadening the stated application scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications about comparing intra-graph and inter-graph kernels. Appendix B.2 attributes weaker performance on node-labeled graphs to ignoring node labels and proposes label-aware walks as future work. Appendix C additionally interprets GRFs++ as positional/structural information for transformers. The original walk-reuse bias qualification remains.

D1.justification: Appendix D replaces v1's promised future code release with a reported open-source implementation and a concrete repository URL. V2 also documents the ViT mask strength, eight-dimensional GraphGPS projections and use of SciPy's Al Mohy implementation. Existing mesh identifiers, hardware disclosure and hyperparameter sweeps are retained; detailed training configurations for the new transformer experiments remain sparse.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for ViT, ImageNet, Places365, GraphGPS and the newly compared GNNs, and discusses relationships to inter-graph kernels and positional encodings. The original positioning within GRF research remains intact. The Dwivedi preprint-to-journal update and removal of the duplicate Beutel reference do not introduce different prior works.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the introductory contribution paragraph, adds explanatory transitions and edits terminology and algorithm notation. The main section sequence remains recognizable. Reproducibility moves from Section 6 to Appendix D, Author Contributions is removed, and an Impact Statement is added. Most retained methodological prose is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column main paper with substantially rearranged displays. V1 Figures 4-5 are combined into v2 Figure 5, and the classification chart is enlarged and expanded to twelve datasets. New baseline tables, runtime displays and non-diffusion plots substantially change the visual presentation, beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for generality and computational usefulness through non-diffusion tests, broader comparisons and direct mesh-runtime scaling against exact computation. It also repairs the MSE derivation, reports classification uncertainty and provides implementation access information. These address important gaps in v1. Benefits are qualified by sparse transformer training details, inconsistent kernel formulas between Section 4 and Appendix B.6, and Table 11's overstated '3 out of 5' claim despite six datasets and ties. These reporting weaknesses limit some additions but do not outweigh the improved mathematical accuracy and broader empirical support.
